items.correct: No — gravity is always attractive; electric/magnetic fields can attract or repel.
items.misconception: Yes, gravity can push objects apart.
items.why: Masses only attract; with charges, like repels like and opposites attract.

items.q: How does a radial field's strength change with distance?
items.correct: It follows an inverse-square law, weakening with distance.
items.misconception: It is the same at all distances.
items.random_wrong: It increases with distance from the source.
items.why: For a point mass or charge, g and E ∝ 1/r², decreasing rapidly as you move away.

items.q: Can field lines cross one another?
items.correct: No — crossing would mean two field directions at one point.
items.misconception: Yes, field lines cross where two fields meet.
items.random_wrong: Field lines that are closer together mean a weaker field.
items.why: Field lines never cross; closer lines indicate a stronger field.
